messages:
anya: heads up — canary for moonshot-compact-v0.3 (int8 build) shows reproducible locale regressions across CJK and RTL samples. quick summary: BLEU -1.8, chrF -2.1, token count +3.5% on our multilang eval set :eyes:
cheng: can you paste a tiny repro (input + baseline vs new) so I can poke at tokenizer/detok?
anya: sure, here's a minimal repro. baseline = moonshot-compact-fp16, candidate = moonshot-compact-int8:
```
INPUT: "昨日の会議で説明したルビ（ふりがな）を送ってください。"\nBASELINE: "昨日の会議で説明したルビ（ふりがな）を送ってください。"\nCANDIDATE: "昨日の会議で説明したルビ （ふりがな）を送ってください。"  # extra space before parentheses

INPUT: "הוא אמר (תגובת דוגמה) שאפשר לבדוק."\nBASELINE: "הוא אמר (תגובת דוגמה) שאפשר לבדוק."\nCANDIDATE: "הוא אמר )תגובת דוגמה( שאפשר לבדוק."  # brackets mirrored / order flipped in candidate
```
koji: interesting — that extra space in ja looks like a token-boundary shift, but the hebrew bracket flip smells like bidi/detokenization bug after quantized kernel changes. can you run token dump for the japanese example?
anya: ran tokenizer dump (new vs baseline):
```
# baseline token ids (ja): [1234,987,45,2001]  -> tokens: ["昨日","の","会議","で"...]
# candidate token ids (int8): [1234,987,45, 99999,2001] -> extra 99999 token corresponds to a narrow-space (U+2009) insertion
```
nidhi: our eval harness flagged ~4% of ja testcases with unexpected whitespace insertions; also saw ~0.7% RTL bracket orientation diffs. failing tests: multilang_detok_space_insertion, rtl_bracket_orientation_check. link: <ci job 3141> :warning: \nsam: from infra side — quant config for this build used symmetric per-channel int8 with native fused attention kernels (v2). we enabled the new detokenizer micro-optimizations in the runtime too; both changed at once. suggest we try: 1) run same int8 weights on older detok path, 2) try asymmetric activation scaling, 3) run a float fallback on detok path for canary subset.
rui: can we bisect which change introduced it? commit range?
anya: canary started after deploy: commits 8f3a2bd..a1b9f44. suspect PR #1287 (kernel reorder + detok micro-opt). I'm starting a bisect job now.
canary-bot: canary run summary: 1000 samples, 43 ja space-insertions, 7 he/arab bracket-orient diffs, delta BLEU -1.76, delta chrF -2.13. Full artifact: s3://canary/moonshot/3141592653/report.json
koji: short-term mitigation: mark the new detok micro-opt as opt-out for pkg moonshot-compact-int8 in canary config, and re-run. also add a targeted unit test: assert no insertion around parentheses/ruby annotations for ja.
cheng: I'll add a script to diff tokenizer boundary positions (char-span -> token-span) so we can catch those +2009/200A insertions automatically.
anya: agreed. next steps I propose: 1) revert detok micro-opt in canary today, 2) run bisect for kernel change vs detok change, 3) run int4/q4a smoke to see if regression persists at lower bitwidths, 4) add regression checks to onboarding pipeline (quick char-span diffs). anyone object? :+1: / :thinking:
nidhi: +1. also please tag platform-i18n so they can sanity-check unicode normalization edgecases.
sam: will schedule a rollback window if we need to revert canary flag.
rui: add me to PRs, I'll help trace the kernel change. good catch.
anya: thanks all — I'll open the reproducer issue with the snippets above and link bisect results when ready. ping me if you want to triage live. :thumbsup:
